title: Problem within a bounded setting
template: Within {scope}, {problem} remains consequential for {stakeholder}.
description: Open a paper by locating a consequential problem inside an explicit setting or population.
notes: Support consequential claims nearby and avoid implying universal importance.

title: Shift in scholarly attention
template: Recent work on {topic} has shifted attention from {earlier_focus} toward {current_focus}.
description: Describe a bounded change in the emphasis of a literature without claiming complete consensus.
notes: Define the reviewed literature and time boundary that support the stated shift.

title: Frame an interpretive debate
template: Debate about {concept} turns in part on how {distinction} is drawn.
description: Introduce an interpretive dispute through the conceptual distinction organizing it.
notes: In part prevents the distinction from being presented as the debate's sole dimension.

title: Frame an engineering trade-off
template: For {system}, the practical challenge is to balance {objective_a} against {objective_b} under {constraint}.
description: Frame an engineering or design problem as an explicit trade-off under a real constraint.
notes: Verify that the objectives genuinely conflict in the defined operating context.

title: Describe sample selection
template: We selected {population} using {sampling_method} during {period}.
description: Report the target group, sampling approach, and collection period without implying representativeness.
notes: Describe eligibility, exclusions, recruitment, and response where relevant.

title: Describe a quantitative model
template: We estimated {model} with {outcome} as the outcome and {predictors} as prespecified predictors.
description: State a quantitative model, outcome, and predictor set while marking prespecification accurately.
notes: Remove prespecified unless the predictor set was fixed before the relevant analysis.

title: Describe qualitative analysis
template: We analyzed {material} using {analytic_approach}, iteratively refining {coding_framework}.
description: Report qualitative material, analytic approach, and the iterative development of interpretation.
notes: Describe researcher roles, reflexivity, disagreement handling, and software where relevant.

title: Describe system evaluation
template: We evaluated {system} against {benchmark} using {metric} under {condition}.
description: Report the evaluated system, comparison benchmark, metric, and operating condition.
notes: State dataset partitions, repetitions, hardware, and uncertainty when they affect comparability.

title: Align method with question
template: We chose {method} because it directly addresses {question} at the level of {unit}.
description: Justify a method through its fit with the research question and unit of analysis.
notes: Directly addresses means fit to the question, not proof that the method is uniquely best.

title: Justify triangulation
template: Combining {method_a} with {method_b} allows {aspect_a} and {aspect_b} to be examined separately.
description: Explain the complementary contribution of two methods without assuming convergence in advance.
notes: Do not claim validation merely because two methods were used.

title: Justify sensitivity analysis
template: We varied {assumption} to assess whether {claim} depended on {uncertain_choice}.
description: Connect a sensitivity analysis to the assumption or analytic choice it probes.
notes: Specify the plausible range and why it addresses the relevant uncertainty.

title: Justify corpus boundaries
template: The corpus was limited to {scope} so that {feature} could be compared under {shared_condition}.
description: Explain how a corpus boundary enables a valid or interpretable comparison.
notes: Also disclose what the boundary excludes and how that limits interpretation.

title: Report threshold and interval
template: For {outcome}, {result} did not meet {decision_threshold}; the interval remained compatible with {possibility}.
description: Report a threshold-based null result while retaining what the uncertainty interval permits.
notes: Give the estimate, interval, threshold, and analysis context; do not conclude no effect.

title: Report equivalence result
template: The equivalence analysis yielded {result}, supporting equivalence within the prespecified margin of {margin}.
description: State an equivalence conclusion only from an analysis and margin designed for that purpose.
notes: Use only when the margin was justified and the analysis satisfies its assumptions.

title: Report unresolved imprecision
template: Across {scope}, {estimate} was too imprecise to resolve whether {claim}.
description: Explain that an estimate leaves a substantive question unresolved because precision is limited.
notes: State the interval or sensitivity range showing why the question remains unresolved.

title: Bound an absence observation
template: No instances of {phenomenon} were observed in {scope}; this {result} does not establish absence beyond that scope.
description: Report that an event was not observed while preventing an unsupported universal absence claim.
notes: Consider detection limits, sample size, search strategy, and opportunities for observation.

title: Report a scoped association
template: Within {scope}, {estimate} indicates an association between {variable_a} and {variable_b}.
description: Report an empirical association with its population or analytic scope attached.
notes: Include direction, scale, uncertainty, and adjustment set where relevant.

title: Report adjusted association
template: After adjustment for {covariates}, {finding} remained associated with {outcome}.
description: Describe an adjusted association without implying that adjustment removes every source of bias.
notes: Do not replace associated with affected, influenced, or caused.

title: Report a graded pattern
template: Across {exposure_levels}, {pattern} was observed for {outcome}.
description: Describe a graded or dose-related observational pattern without assigning a causal mechanism.
notes: A gradient can support but does not alone establish causation.

title: Separate prediction from explanation
template: In {evaluation_scope}, {estimate} shows that {predictor} improves prediction of {outcome} relative to {benchmark}.
description: Report predictive improvement against a benchmark without claiming explanation or intervention benefit.
notes: Name the held-out population, horizon, metric, and uncertainty when available.

title: Temporal order is not causation
template: Although {finding} establishes temporal order, it does not by itself identify {cause} as a cause of {outcome}.
description: Prevent a temporal sequence from being upgraded automatically to a causal relation.
notes: State confounding, selection, reverse pathways, or design assumptions relevant to identification.

title: Bound residual confounding
template: Because {unmeasured_factor} may account for part of {finding}, {estimate} should be interpreted as associational.
description: Tie an observational interpretation to a specific unresolved source of confounding.
notes: Do not imply that measured adjustment eliminates unmeasured or poorly measured confounding.

title: Prediction does not imply intervention effect
template: Although {result} improves prediction of {outcome}, it does not show that changing {predictor} would change that outcome.
description: Separate predictive usefulness from a counterfactual intervention claim.
notes: A causal claim needs an identified intervention, comparator, estimand, and assumptions.

title: Mediation remains unestablished
template: The observed change in {mechanism} is compatible with mediation, but {evidence} does not isolate that pathway from {alternative}.
description: Describe mechanism-compatible evidence without declaring a mediated causal pathway.
notes: Mechanism measurement and temporal order alone do not identify mediation.

title: Attribute a source claim
template: According to {source}, {claim} within {scope}.
description: Keep a proposition attached to the source that advances it and to its stated boundary.
notes: Retain the citation and do not present the attributed claim as an uncontested fact.

title: Attribute an interpretation
template: {source} interprets {evidence} as support for {claim}, while acknowledging {limitation}.
description: Represent a source's interpretation together with the limitation it recognizes.
notes: Replace source with a grammatical author reference and preserve the citation boundary.

title: Attribute a working definition
template: As {source} defines it, {term} refers to {definition}.
description: Introduce a source-specific definition without implying that it is the only accepted usage.
notes: Preserve quotation marks when wording is copied exactly; otherwise paraphrase and cite.

title: Separate source positions
template: Where {source_a} treats {concept} as {position_a}, {source_b} treats it as {position_b}.
description: Contrast two attributed positions while preserving ownership of each proposition.
notes: Use parallel descriptions and avoid caricaturing either position.

title: Restate a source proposition
template: {source} argues that {claim}; here, that position is restated in relation to {current_focus}.
description: Signal that a source proposition is being paraphrased and connected to the current argument.
notes: Draft independently from semantic notes, preserve the citation, and avoid close structural imitation.

title: Build on an attributed distinction
template: Building on {source}, the present account distinguishes {concept_a} from {concept_b}.
description: Retain attribution when a current argument adopts or develops a source's conceptual distinction.
notes: Clarify which part comes from the source and which part is the current writer's development.

title: Summarize a proposed mechanism
template: The mechanism proposed in {source} can be summarized as {summary}.
description: Provide an attributed summary of a source's mechanism without adopting it as established fact.
notes: Preserve qualifications and causal status; quote instead if distinctive wording is indispensable.

title: Mark proposition preservation
template: Without reproducing {source}'s wording, this account retains its proposition that {claim}.
description: Make explicit that expression changes while the attributed proposition remains source-dependent.
notes: This pattern does not remove citation duties and should not be used to disguise copied expression.

title: Report estimate and interval
template: For {outcome}, {estimate} was accompanied by an uncertainty interval from {lower_bound} to {upper_bound}.
description: Report an estimate together with the endpoints of its stated uncertainty interval.
notes: State interval type, level, scale, and units; preserve endpoint signs and precision.

title: Report sensitivity range
template: Across the sensitivity analyses, {estimate} ranged from {lower_result} to {upper_result}.
description: Summarize how an estimate varies across prespecified or justified sensitivity analyses.
notes: Name the varied assumptions; a narrow range does not address biases shared by all analyses.

title: Report heterogeneous uncertainty
template: Uncertainty was greatest for {subgroup}, where {result} remained compatible with {possibilities}.
description: Locate imprecision in a subgroup and state the substantive possibilities it leaves open.
notes: Avoid treating subgroup estimates as different without a relevant contrast or interaction test.

title: Bound measurement uncertainty
template: Because {measurement_issue} affects {estimate}, the reported value should be read within {uncertainty_boundary}.
description: Connect a known measurement limitation to the boundary on an empirical estimate.
notes: State direction or magnitude of measurement error only when evidence supports it.

title: Interpret a recurring qualitative pattern
template: Across {source}, {pattern} recurred in accounts of {experience}.
description: Report a recurring pattern across qualitative materials while retaining its evidential source.
notes: Describe variation and show how the pattern was developed from the material.

title: Retain a deviant case
template: {finding} was common, but {counterexample} shows that it was not uniform across {scope}.
description: Interpret a common qualitative finding while preserving a counterexample or deviant case.
notes: Do not reduce frequency to prevalence unless the design supports quantitative inference.

title: Offer a bounded qualitative interpretation
template: {evidence} suggests {claim}, although {alternative} remains plausible.
description: Offer an interpretation grounded in qualitative evidence while keeping an alternative account live.
notes: Make the link between evidence and interpretation explicit rather than relying on suggests alone.

title: Locate interpretation reflexively
template: Because {researcher_position} shaped access to {material}, {finding} is interpreted within {scope}.
description: Connect researcher position or access to a bounded interpretation of qualitative material.
notes: Be specific about access, relationship, or analytic standpoint; avoid generic reflexivity claims.

title: Acknowledge and revise
template: We thank the reviewer for identifying {issue}; we revised {location} to {revision}.
description: Acknowledge a concrete review point and state the corresponding manuscript revision.
notes: Describe the change precisely; do not claim resolution when the concern remains partly open.

title: Respectfully retain a decision
template: We respectfully retain {decision} because {reason}; the manuscript now clarifies {boundary}.
description: Explain a reasoned disagreement with a reviewer while adding a clarifying boundary.
notes: Address the strongest version of the concern and keep tone factual rather than defensive.

title: Report added analysis
template: In response to {comment}, we added {analysis}; {result} is now reported in {location}.
description: Connect a review comment to a new analysis, its result, and its manuscript location.
notes: Do not imply that the added analysis validates claims beyond its design and assumptions.

title: Acknowledge a limitation
template: We agree that {limitation} constrains {claim}; this is now stated in {location}.
description: Accept a valid limitation and show where its consequence for a claim is disclosed.
notes: The revised manuscript should state the inferential consequence, not merely name the limitation.

title: Contribution to a bounded gap
template: This study addresses {gap} by examining {question} in {scope}.
description: State a contribution through the specific gap, question, and scope it addresses.
notes: Avoid first or novel unless a transparent search supports the priority claim.

title: Methodological contribution
template: The study contributes {resource} for examining {question} under {condition}.
description: Describe a method, dataset, framework, or resource contribution without universal superiority claims.
notes: State availability, validation, and scope separately when relevant.

title: Empirical contribution from convergence
template: By combining {evidence}, the study provides support for {claim} across {scope}.
description: State an empirical contribution based on convergent evidence and a named scope.
notes: Explain independence and relevance of the evidence streams before invoking convergence.

title: Conceptual contribution
template: The analysis refines {concept} by distinguishing {dimension_a} from {dimension_b}.
description: State a conceptual contribution as a precise distinction rather than an unsupported novelty claim.
notes: Show how the distinction changes analysis or interpretation, and cite prior formulations.
